description: Hammer excitation: the temporal force curve (5 Gaussians per velocity level), the spatial hammer shape, and the excitation-energy loudness factors.

domains.title: Temporal excitation curves (base levels)
domains.write: param.set {parameter: gauss, key_no, values} (the GET shape); one level of one pitch: REST POST /set_string_excitation/<pitch_no> (no registry command)
domains.shape: per pitch: {velocity level (the 6 base levels 0,5,31,63,95,127): {component 0..4: {mu, sigma, volume, shift}}}
domains.stored_vs_effective: The 6 base levels are stored; the 128 levels the engine uses are linear interpolations between them. The force is the sum of 5 Gaussians with a per-component ReLU on the GPU (the GPU formula is the one used in synthesis; Python calculate() clips the total instead). In conserve mode the curve carries SHAPE: the coefficient divides the curve integral out, so loudness is set by c*m*v (excitation_energy). A curve edit is a shape edit: it clears output_scale_calibrated (recalibration trigger).

fields.name: mu
fields.units: x-units = segments of mode_iteration/sr (1.333 ms at 64 samples/cycle, 48 kHz)
fields.range: finite; the GPU writes segments 0..6 of the 8-segment window (9.33 ms written at 64/48 kHz)
fields.meaning: Peak time of one Gaussian component; mu up -> peak later.

fields.name: sigma
fields.meaning: Width of one Gaussian component; sigma up -> wider and duller; a shorter pulse gives a louder transient at the same impulse.

fields.name: volume
fields.units: dimensionless engine amplitude (no physical force unit)
fields.meaning: Peak amplitude of one Gaussian component (curve shape; the conserve-mode coefficient divides the curve integral out).

fields.name: shift
fields.meaning: Vertical (baseline) offset of one component = its ReLU threshold offset; assert its effect against the GPU force buffer, never Python calculate().

domains.title: Temporal excitation curves (all 128 levels)
domains.write: read-only in practice (no documented POST form; edit the base levels through gauss)
domains.shape: per pitch: {velocity level 0..127: {component 0..4: {mu, sigma, volume, shift}}} (same fields as gauss)
domains.stored_vs_effective: Levels other than the 6 base levels are interpolated (derived) from the base levels.

domains.title: Temporal excitation curves (flat array)
domains.write: read-only in practice (no documented POST form)
domains.shape: flat array per pitch; REST_API says 100 values (the GPU per-level layout is [mu x5, sigma x5, volume x5, shift x5]); length vs 6 base levels is a doc conflict (see _index.json)
domains.stored_vs_effective: Same stored base-level data as gauss, flattened.

domains.title: One velocity level of one pitch's curves
domains.read: param.get {parameter: gauss, key_no: <pitch>} (no GET of its own)
domains.write: none in the registry; REST POST /set_string_excitation/<pitch_no> {level, curves: {component: {sigma, mu, volume, shift}}}
domains.key_space: one piano pitch (path) + one velocity level (body)
domains.stored_vs_effective: Writes the same stored curves as gauss; the state_changed event for this domain carries after = null (the client refetches the pitch). Shape edit: clears output_scale_calibrated.

fields.name: level
fields.meaning: The velocity level whose curves are set.

fields.name: curves
fields.units: per component: mu / sigma / volume / shift as in gauss
fields.range: sigma > 0; every field finite (else 400 before any state change)
fields.meaning: Gaussian component parameters of that level, keyed by component index.

domains.title: Spatial hammer shape
domains.read: param.get {parameter: hammer, key_no}; the exact per-node shape: REST GET /get_hammer_shape/<pitch_no> (no registry command)
domains.write: param.set {parameter: hammer, key_no, values} (values = {pitch: {hammer: {...}}}, the GET shape; GET -> POST is the identity); REST POST /set_hammer_shape/<pitch_no> {shape, width, position, sharpness}
domains.shape: {hammer: {hammer_shape, hammer_width, hammer_position, hammer_sharpness, hammer_radius, hammer_width_effective}} per pitch
domains.stored_vs_effective: hammer_width is STORED; hammer_width_effective (rendered = max(stored, 1.05*dx)) and hammer_radius are derived, read-only. A legacy sub-floor stored width is kept as stored until a real width edit floors it. Read-only fields are ignored on POST, a field equal to the stored value is not an edit, an unknown field -> 416. Hammer geometry edits are shape edits: they clear output_scale_calibrated.

fields.name: hammer_width
fields.range: finite; the rendered width has a floor (doc conflict: 1.05*dx in REST_API vs 3*dx in Basic OVERVIEW)
fields.meaning: Hammer contact width; width up -> spectral centroid down (duller).

fields.name: hammer_width_effective
fields.meaning: The width the engine renders = max(stored, 1.05*dx); read-only.

fields.name: hammer_position
fields.meaning: Strike point along the main string; striking at L/n suppresses the n-th partial (comb filter).

fields.name: hammer_sharpness
fields.meaning: Curvature parameter of the hammer profile; its centroid direction is UNKNOWN (needs a one-time measurement per the test strategy).

fields.name: hammer_shape
fields.meaning: Profile function of the hammer; ignored on a param.set (read-only field).

fields.name: hammer_radius
fields.units: dimensionless ratio (pack() converts radius to a ratio for the kernel)
fields.meaning: Arc radius of the circular profile derived from width and sharpness; read-only.

domains.title: Combined hammer + temporal excitation
domains.write: param.set {parameter: excitation, key_no, values} (sigma > 0 is enforced on this route)
domains.shape: per pitch: the hammer GET block plus an 'excitation' flat array of the base-level curve parameters
domains.stored_vs_effective: Combines the stored hammer and gauss data; see those domains.

fields.name: hammer
fields.meaning: The hammer block of the pitch (see domain hammer).

fields.name: excitation
fields.meaning: Flat array of the temporal curve parameters (see gauss_flat).

domains.title: Excitation energy (loudness factors)
domains.read: none in the registry; REST GET /excitation_energy
domains.write: none in the registry for a direct edit (REST POST /excitation_energy, any subset of the fields); calibration.synthesis / calibration.acoustic change hammer_mass
domains.key_space: hammer_mass: piano pitch; hammer_speeds: the 6 velocity breakpoints; excitation_impulse_calibration: global
domains.stored_vs_effective: Stored model values, persisted per preset; the engine uses the composed per-(string, level) coefficient c*m*v*G/(temporal*spatial). These are LEVEL edits (by-design loudness): they do NOT clear output_scale_calibrated, and a re-calibration keeps the mass/speed/c level (impulse reference). Global loudness belongs to the runtime volume, not here.

fields.name: hammer_mass
fields.range: physical range 2-20 g (0.002-0.020 kg); /rescale_hammer_mass and every calibration pass move all masses into it with one common factor
fields.meaning: Per-pitch hammer mass, the per-pitch loudness lever (mass up -> louder); one value per pitch, every velocity level.

fields.name: hammer_speeds
fields.range: UNKNOWN (defaults ppp 0.3 -> fff 5.5 m/s, linear between the 6 breakpoints)
fields.meaning: Six per-velocity-level hammer speeds (at level_indices); the per-level loudness (speed up -> louder).

fields.name: excitation_impulse_calibration
fields.meaning: Global calibration constant c mapping the impulse m*v to engine amplitude; a clean global rescale.

fields.name: level_indices
fields.meaning: The velocity breakpoints the 6 hammer_speeds belong to.

domains.title: Keybed thump string (dev-thump1)
domains.read: param.get {parameter: thump, key_no: all} -> {available, config, engine_pool, engine_supported}
domains.write: param.set {parameter: thump, key_no: all, values: {enabled?, gain?, trim_db?: {key: dB}, level_coeff?: [pp, p, mf, f, ff]}} (trim_db merges per key; 0 removes; level_coeff is the whole list of 5)
domains.key_space: global config; trim_db keyed by piano pitch 21-108
domains.shape: {enabled: bool, pitch: int (the thump pitch, default 20), gain: float, trim_db: {pitch: dB}, level_coeff: [5 floats]}
domains.stored_vs_effective: Stored in model_parameters.thump (saved with the preset; absent = no thump string). Effective per-key engine gain = gain * 10^(trim_db/20), 0 for every key when disabled. level_coeff multiplies the thump string's own excitation coefficient at velocities 5/31/63/95/127 (linear between levels; independent of enabled). The thump string's own physics (hammer_mass = keybed mass, gauss sigma/mu = contact time/delay, deck row = rim coupling) are ordinary parameters of the thump pitch. Excluded from loudness calibration.

fields.name: enabled
fields.meaning: Every key note-on also excites the shared thump string with the key's velocity.

fields.name: gain
fields.meaning: Global gain on the thump-string coefficient (impulse).

fields.name: trim_db
fields.meaning: Per-key trim of the thump gain.

fields.name: level_coeff
fields.range: 5 values 0-10 (rule thump.level_coeff), default 1.0; order pp, p, mf, f, ff = velocities 5, 31, 63, 95, 127
fields.meaning: Thump force coefficient per velocity level for all keys (0 = no thump at that level). Scales the thump string's coefficient row; between levels the force moves linearly. Low Thump pane.

domains.title: Per-pitch excitation (hammer / friction bow)
domains.stored_vs_effective: Stored in the preset: model_parameters.excitation_mode = {bow: [pitch, ...]} (absent = every key hammer; old presets load unchanged). Saved, loaded and switched with the library; pushed to the engine (read at note-on) on every load / switch / edit. An edit goes through edit_commit: rule excitation_mode.modes (int 0..1), state_changed{excitation_mode}, one undo step per edit, 409 on a read-only original.

fields.name: modes
fields.units: per pitch: 0 = hammer (one-shot strike), 1 = friction bow (sustains while held, velocity = bow speed)
fields.meaning: Excitation type of each pitch of the active preset.

domains.title: Friction-bow parameters (per pitch)
domains.write: param.bow {key_no, values} = param.set {parameter: bow, key_no, values}
domains.key_space: piano pitch (shared by the pitch's unison strings)
domains.shape: {pitch: {speed, force, position, tilt}}; a write may send {field: value} for every key of key_no
domains.stored_vs_effective: Stored in the preset: model_parameters.bow.pitches = {pitch: {speed, force, position, tilt}} for the edited pitches only; an absent pitch = the defaults (speed 0.5, force 0.5 x the register scale (x0.6 at pitches 46-55, linear to x1 at 40 and 60), position 1, tilt 0.3). GET returns the effective values. Pushed to the engine (BowController, per pitch -> the pitch's strings) on load / switch / edit / undo. A MIDI controller assignment (dev-midictl) moves the ENGINE values within its own range without changing the stored ones; velocity -> speed (default) or force is such an assignment, applied at note-on.

fields.name: speed
fields.units: normalised; x BOW_SPEED_SCALE engine displacement per sub-step
fields.meaning: Bow speed; the level follows it linearly. Default: set by the MIDI velocity (velocity / 127) unless the velocity is assigned to force.

fields.name: force
fields.units: fraction of the Schelleng maximum force (2 Z vb / (beta (mu_s - mu_d)) at beta 0.125)
fields.meaning: Bow pressure. 0.5 = the middle of the Helmholtz window; low = airy / surface sound, high = raucous.

fields.name: position
fields.units: multiple of the hammer point's distance from the string end
fields.meaning: Bow contact point; 1 = the hammer point (beta ~0.12-0.15), larger = towards sul tasto. Kept inside the main string.

fields.name: tilt
fields.meaning: Bow tilt, one physical control: contact width = ribbon x (1 - 0.7 tilt) of the main string (min 3, max 16 points), friction-curve softness v0 = vb (0.2 + 2.8 tilt), string HF loss x 2^(1.2 (tilt - 0.3)).

domains.title: Friction-bow ribbon (per preset)
domains.shape: {max_width} (the GET adds limits, fields, engaged_strings, velocity {field, curve}, engine_supported)
domains.stored_vs_effective: Stored in the preset: model_parameters.bow.max_width (absent = 0.035). The kernel converts ribbon x (1 - 0.7 tilt) x main-string length to contact points, at least 3, at most 16, inside the main string.

fields.name: max_width
fields.range: 0..0.5 (rule bow_settings.max_width); default 0.035 (CPU model: 0.06 slips twice per period on C2 at tilt 0.3)
fields.meaning: Hair ribbon of a flat bow; tilt narrows it. 0 = a one-point contact.
